q.s: In the Rig Vedic period, the Kikata tribe is believed to have lived in which region?
q.x: The Rig Veda places the Kikatas in south Bihar, the later Magadha.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the Panchajana (five tribes) of the Rig Veda?
q.x: The Panchajana were the Anu, Druhyu, Yadu, Turvasa and Puru; the Bharatas, tribe of Sudas, were separate.

q.s: In the early Vedic polity, the Gramani was:
o: Head of the village / fighting band
q.x: The Gramani headed the village or fighting band; the Kulapa was head of the family.

q.s: Which of the following statements about ancient Indian guilds (shrenis) is correct?
o: The Satapatha Brahmana uses the term setthi for a usurer
The head of a guild was called the jetthaka or pamukha
The king appointed and controlled the heads of guilds
Guilds first appeared only in the Gupta period
q.x: The guild head was the jetthaka/pamukha and guilds were autonomous; the Satapatha Brahmana calls the usurer kusidin.

q.s: Salihundam in Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh is known as a centre of:
q.x: Salihundam was a Buddhist (Vajrayana) centre, not a Jaina one.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six paramitas (perfections) of the Bodhisattva?
q.x: The six paramitas are dana, sila, kshanti, virya, dhyana and prajna; moksha is not one of them.

q.s: According to the Mahavamsa, which monk took Buddhism from Andhra to Sri Lanka?
q.x: The Mahavamsa credits Mahadeva Bhikshu of Andhra.

q.s: Ashoka sent which of the following to Sri Lanka to spread Buddhism?
q.x: Ashoka's son Mahinda and daughter Sanghamitta took Buddhism to Sri Lanka.

q.s: The Dhamek Stupa at Sarnath attained its present form during the period of the:
q.x: Dhamek's present form belongs to the Gupta period (c. 500 CE); Piprahwa and Sanchi are far older.

q.s: The Charvaka (Lokayata) school accepted which of the following as the only valid means of knowledge?
q.x: Accepting only perception, the Charvakas rejected Vedic ritual and the afterlife.

q.s: Which Ikshvaku royal women are known for patronising Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda?
q.x: Ikshvaku queens such as Chantisiri and Bodhisiri patronised Buddhist monuments at Nagarjunakonda.

q.s: Under the Mauryas, the king's regular share of the produce was called:
q.x: Bhaga, normally one-sixth, was the regular share; pranaya was an emergency tax and sita the income from crown land.

q.s: In the Mauryan revenue system, income from crown land was known as:
q.x: Sita was income from crown land; bali was an additional levy or tribute.

q.s: In Mauryan administration, the Rajukas were mainly responsible for:
q.x: The Rajukas handled land survey and assessment and also had judicial powers; frontier forts were under the Antapala.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Mauryan local administration is correct?
o: A city's municipality was headed by the Nagaraka
The Rakshinas were in charge of frontier forts
The Gramika was a district-level officer
The Rajukas had no judicial powers
q.x: The Nagaraka headed the city; the Gramika was the village headman, the Rakshinas the police and frontier forts were under the Antapala.

q.s: Which is regarded as the largest stupa in India, located in East Champaran district of Bihar?
q.x: Kesariya in East Champaran is the largest (about 104 ft).

q.s: Harisena's Allahabad Prashasti was composed in praise of:
q.x: The Allahabad Pillar Prashasti by Harisena praises Samudragupta, equating him with Kubera, Varuna, Indra and Yama.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Guptas is correct?
o: The Allahabad Prashasti is in praise of Chandragupta II
The Narada smriti survives only in fragments
Gupta kings bore titles such as Maharajadhiraja and Paramabhattaraka
Harisena was the court poet of Skandagupta
q.x: Gupta rulers took high imperial titles; the Narada smriti survives in full and Harisena was Samudragupta's poet.

q.s: At Nalanda, Hiuen Tsang studied the Yogashastra under the teacher:
q.x: Hiuen Tsang studied the Yogashastra under Silabhadra at Nalanda.

q.s: Which Pallava ruler was praised by Hiuen Tsang?
q.x: Hiuen Tsang praised Narasimhavarman I, besides Harsha and Pulakesin II.

q.s: Under Mubarak Shah Khalji, who led the invasion of Warangal in 1318?
q.x: Khusrau Khan led the 1318 invasion after Kakatiya tribute stopped following 1316.

q.s: The famous Madrasa of Mahmud Gawan is located at:
q.x: The Mahmud Gawan Madrasa is at Bidar, the later Bahmani capital.

q.s: Which mosque is known for its fully covered courtyard and a large dome?
q.x: The Gulbarga Jama Masjid is unique for having its whole courtyard covered.

q.s: In Akbar's mansabdari system, the term 'Sawar' denoted:
o: Number of horsemen to be maintained
q.x: Sawar indicated the cavalry to be maintained; zat denoted personal rank and pay.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Akbar's mansabdari system is correct?
o: Mansabs were hereditary and passed to the son
Sawar denoted the personal rank of the noble
Zat denoted the personal rank and pay of the mansabdar
q.x: Zat was personal rank and pay; mansabs were not hereditary and lapsed to the state.

q.s: In which year did Aurangzeb reimpose the jizya?
q.x: Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya in 1679; Akbar had abolished it in 1564.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of Aurangzeb?
q.x: Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya (1679); Akbar had abolished it.

q.s: Saadatullah Khan, who made the Carnatic nawabship hereditary, named which relative as his heir?
q.x: Saadatullah Khan named his nephew Dost Ali heir without the Nizam's approval.

q.s: Which of the following traveller–account pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Peter Mundy – Famine under Shah Jahan
q.x: The Remonstrantie was Pelsaert's; Careri traced the silver route c. 1690.

q.s: In Mughal agrarian society, the term 'Muzarian' referred to:
o: Tenants cultivating land held by others
q.x: Muzarian were tenants; khud-kasht were resident cultivators and pahi-kasht cultivated in another village.

q.s: The Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad is the tomb of:
q.x: It is the tomb of Aurangzeb's wife Rabia-ud-Daurani, built by their son Azam Shah.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Bibi ka Maqbara is correct?
o: Its architect Ata-ullah was the son of Ustad Isa
It was built by Aurangzeb's son Azam Shah
It is the tomb of Aurangzeb's mother
q.x: Azam Shah built it at Aurangabad for his mother Rabia-ud-Daurani; Ata-ullah was the son of Ustad Ahmad Lahori.

q.s: 'The Agrarian System of Mughal India, 1556-1707' was written by:
q.x: Irfan Habib wrote it (1963); Moreland wrote India at the Death of Akbar.

q.s: Which of the following books was NOT written by Jadunath Sarkar?
o: India at the Death of Akbar
q.x: India at the Death of Akbar (1920) was written by W.H. Moreland.

q.s: Which Qutb Shahi ruler, the first Urdu poet with a diwan, built the Charminar?
q.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built the Charminar (1591) and was the first Urdu poet with a diwan.

q.s: The Charyapada songs are associated with the:
q.x: The Charyapada are songs of the Buddhist Siddhacharyas; the manuscript was found by Haraprasad Shastri in Nepal.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Carnatic Music Trinity?
q.x: The Trinity is Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri; Annamacharya was an earlier composer.

q.s: Jalaluddin Tabrizi, the Sufi saint of Bengal, belonged to which order?
q.x: Jalaluddin Tabrizi was a Suhrawardi saint.

q.s: The Firdausi Sufi order of Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri flourished in:
q.x: The Firdausi order flourished in Bihar.

q.s: Which of the following Sufi term–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Fana – Annihilation of the self in God
Urs – Death anniversary of a saint
q.x: Zikr is the remembrance of God; chilla is the 40-day retreat.

q.s: The Ottoman Turks captured Constantinople, closing the overland route to the East, in the year:
q.x: The fall of Constantinople in 1453 pushed Europeans to seek a sea route to India.

q.s: Fort Geldria, the Dutch headquarters on the Coromandel coast till 1690, was located at:
q.x: Fort Geldria was at Pulicat, the Dutch Coromandel headquarters till 1690.

q.s: The English ship Globe reached Machilipatnam in 1611 under the command of:
q.x: The Globe reached Machilipatnam in 1611 under Captain Anthony Hippon, with Peter Floris as merchant.

q.s: Permission for the first English factory at Machilipatnam was given by which Golconda ruler?
q.x: The permission came from Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.

q.s: The new rifle whose greased cartridges became the immediate cause of the Revolt of 1857 was the:
q.x: The Enfield rifle replaced the Brown Bess; its cartridge had to be bitten off.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a centre where sepoys were trained in the Enfield rifle in 1857?
q.x: Training in the Enfield rifle was held at Dum Dum, Ambala and Sialkot.

q.s: 'Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind' on the causes of the Revolt of 1857 was written by:
q.x: Sir Syed's work (1859) was the first Indian-language work on the revolt's causes.

q.s: Which of the following statements about writings on the Revolt of 1857 is correct?
o: V.D. Savarkar's 'The Indian War of Independence, 1857' was published in 1909
Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind was written by Bahadur Shah Zafar
P.E. Roberts called the revolt a national war of independence
Sir Syed did not count the absence of Indians in the Legislative Council as a cause
q.x: Savarkar's book came out in 1909; Roberts called it a sepoy mutiny and Sir Syed did list the absence of Indians in the Council.

q.s: During the Revolt of 1857, the attack on the Hyderabad Residency was led by:
q.x: Turrebaz Khan, with Maulvi Allauddin, led the attack; Salar Jung I and the Nizam stayed pro-British.

q.s: In 1858, Gwalior fell to the rebels because its troops went over to:
q.x: Though the Scindia stayed loyal, his troops joined the Rani of Jhansi.

q.s: After the Revolt of 1857, Bahadur Shah II was exiled to:
q.x: He was tried and exiled to Rangoon, where he died in 1862; Nana Saheb escaped to Nepal.

q.s: Which leader of 1857 was betrayed and executed in April 1859?
q.x: Tantia Tope was betrayed by Man Singh and executed in April 1859.

q.s: During the Revolt of 1857, the educated middle class largely:
q.x: Seeing British rule as modernising, the educated middle class stayed neutral.

q.s: The Queen's Proclamation of 1 November 1858 was read out by Lord Canning at a durbar held at:
q.x: Canning read it at Allahabad; it is called the Magna Carta of the Indian people.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Queen's Proclamation of 1858 is correct?
o: It transferred power from the Crown to the Company
It was read out by Lord Dalhousie at Calcutta
It disclaimed any further annexation of princely states
q.x: It was issued on 1 November 1858, read by Canning at Allahabad, and transferred power from the Company to the Crown.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Pitt's India Act, 1784 is correct?
o: It reduced the Governor-General's council to three members
It gave political affairs to the Court of Directors
Its Board of Control included the Governor-General
It ended the system of double government
q.x: The Act cut the council to three; political affairs went to the Board of Control and double government lasted till 1858.

q.s: The system of 'double government' created by Pitt's India Act, 1784 was ended by the:
q.x: Double government ended with the Government of India Act, 1858.

q.s: The 'Blue Rebellion' of 1859-60 in Bengal was a revolt of ryots against:
q.x: The ryots of Bengal refused to grow indigo for the European planters.

q.s: Which of the following movements did NOT take place in Bengal?
q.x: The Deccan Riots (1875) were in Maharashtra.

q.s: The first census of India (1872), though non-synchronous, was held during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: The 1872 census was under Lord Mayo; the first synchronous census was in 1881 under Ripon.

q.s: Financial decentralisation in British India began with the Resolution of 1870 of:
q.x: Mayo's 1870 Resolution began financial decentralisation.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the four-point social agenda of the Prarthana Samaj?
q.x: Its agenda was disapproval of caste, women's education, widow remarriage and raising the age of marriage.

q.s: Which of the following book–author pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Orion was written by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

q.s: Who wrote 'Annihilation of Caste'?
q.x: Ambedkar wanted caste annihilated; Gandhi wanted Hinduism reformed from within.

q.s: The Arya Samaj was founded by Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 at:
q.x: It was founded at Bombay in 1875; its ten principles were finalised at Lahore in 1877.

q.s: Dayananda Saraswati's 'Satyarth Prakash' was written in which language?
q.x: Satyarth Prakash ('The Light of Truth') was written in Hindi.

q.s: The Arya Samaj satyagraha against the Nizam's curbs on religious and civil rights in Hyderabad State took place in:
q.x: The satyagraha was held in 1938-39.

q.s: During the Revolt of 1857, Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was in the Company's:
q.x: He served in the judicial service; he later wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind (1859).

q.s: Which of the following statements about Sir Syed Ahmad Khan is correct?
o: He defended and promoted Urdu in the Hindi-Urdu controversy
He founded the Darul Uloom at Deoband
He was in the Company's military service in 1857
q.x: Sir Syed defended Urdu; he wrote Asbab in 1859 and founded the Aligarh college, not Deoband.

q.s: Vande Mataram was first sung at a session of the Indian National Congress held at Calcutta in:
q.x: It was first sung at the 1896 Calcutta session.

q.s: Kadambini Ganguly, who addressed the 1890 Congress session, was one of the first women graduates of:
q.x: She was among the first women graduates of Calcutta University.

q.s: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was launched against:
q.x: The revenue hike caused it; the women of Bardoli gave Patel the title 'Sardar'.

q.s: Who gave Vallabhbhai Patel the title 'Sardar'?
q.x: The title came from the women of Bardoli during the 1928 satyagraha.

q.s: The Telangana armed struggle was finally called off in:
q.x: It went on after the Police Action and was called off in October 1951.

q.s: Doddi Komaraiah, the first martyr of the Telangana armed struggle, was shot in 1946 at:
q.x: He was shot at Kadavendi on 4 July 1946 by the men of the Visnur deshmukh.

q.s: Who is called the 'Father of Communal Electorate' in India?
q.x: Minto, through the 1909 reforms, is called the Father of Communal Electorate.

q.s: The Poona Pact of 1932 replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes with:
q.x: The Poona Pact gave reserved seats in joint electorates.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Gandhi's early movements in India is correct?
o: The Champaran Satyagraha followed the Kheda Satyagraha
He first formulated satyagraha at Champaran
Champaran (1917) was his first civil disobedience in India
His first fast in India was at Champaran
q.x: Champaran (1917) was the first civil disobedience; satyagraha was formulated in South Africa and his first fast came in the Ahmedabad mill strike, 1918.

q.s: The demand for a Constituent Assembly for India was first raised in 1934 by:
q.x: M.N. Roy first raised it in 1934; the Congress adopted the demand in 1935.

q.s: The Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) was proclaimed by Subhas Chandra Bose on:
q.x: It was proclaimed at Singapore on 21 October 1943; Bose had taken over the IIL and INA on 4 July 1943.

q.s: Who was the first and only Indian Governor-General of independent India?
q.x: Rajaji was Governor-General from June 1948 to January 1950, after Mountbatten.

q.s: C. Rajagopalachari founded the Swatantra Party in the year:
q.x: He formed the Swatantra Party in 1959.

q.s: The volunteer force of the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign (1921-22) in Guntur district was called:
q.x: Pedanandipadu's volunteers formed the Shanti Sena; the Ramadandu belonged to the Chirala-Perala movement.

q.s: The no-tax campaigns of 1921-22 in Guntur district were launched after permission was given by the:
q.x: The Delhi AICC of 5 November 1921 allowed provincial committees to start civil disobedience including no-tax.

q.s: Who gave Gandhi a copy of Ruskin's 'Unto This Last' in 1904?
q.x: Henry Polak gave him the book in 1904, which inspired the Phoenix Settlement.

q.s: Which Jain vow is believed to have been added by Mahavira to the four vows of Parshvanatha?
q.x: Parshvanatha taught four vows; Mahavira added brahmacharya.

q.s: Gandhi's idea of civil disobedience, the right to break unjust laws, was influenced by the writings of:
q.x: Thoreau's essay Civil Disobedience shaped it; bread labour came from Tolstoy and Ruskin.

q.s: The Andhra Mahasabha session that voted district-wise because most delegates were from the host district was held in 1917 at:
q.x: At Nellore (1917) 480 of 740 delegates were local, so voting was district-wise.

q.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 retained which domicile rules for Telangana?
q.x: It kept the Mulki rules, so Telangana's domicile safeguards continued after 1956.

q.s: Who moved the merger (Visalandhra) resolution of 1955 in the Andhra Assembly?
q.x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy's resolution was passed unanimously.

q.s: The Six-Point Formula for Andhra Pradesh was announced in the year:
q.x: It came in 1973 after the Jai Andhra agitation; the Presidential Order followed in 1975 and GO 610 in 1985.

q.s: Which of the following year–event pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Six-Point Formula came in 1973; 1985 saw GO 610.

q.s: The Billa Surgam caves were explored in 1884 by:
q.x: Robert Bruce Foote, who found the first Palaeolithic tool at Pallavaram, explored them.

q.s: The Belum Caves, the second-longest cave system in the Indian subcontinent, are located in which district?
q.x: Belum Caves are in the Kurnool region (now Nandyal district).

q.s: Bavari's sixteen disciples, who went from the Godavari region to meet the Buddha, are mentioned in the:
q.x: The Parayana-vagga of the Suttanipata tells the story of Bavari.

q.s: The founder of the Satavahana dynasty, who killed the Kanva king Susarma, was:
q.x: Simuka founded the dynasty and was succeeded by his brother Kanha.

q.s: Devi Naganika, who issued the Naneghat inscription and acted as regent, was the queen of:
q.x: Naganika was the wife of Satakarni I, not Hala.

q.s: Under the Ikshvakus, Nagarjunakonda was known as:
q.x: As Vijayapuri (Sriparvata) it was the Ikshvaku capital.

q.s: The Sinhala Vihara at Nagarjunakonda for monks from Sri Lanka was donated by:
q.x: Upasika Bodhisri built the Sinhala Vihara; Kodabalisri gave a vihara for Mahishasaka monks.

q.s: The Mogalrajapuram cave temples at Vijayawada were excavated by the:
q.x: They are Vishnukundin Brahmanical caves; Cave 4 is the Durga cave with Ardhanarishvara.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Mogalrajapuram caves is correct?
o: The complex consists of eight caves
Navagraha figures appear on the kapota
Cave 4 is the Durga cave with Ardhanarishvara on its back wall
q.x: Cave 4 is the Durga cave; the caves are Brahmanical, five in number, with Trimurti on the kapota.

q.s: The Shore Temple at Mamallapuram was built by:
q.x: The Shore Temple was built by Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha).

q.s: Which of the following temples was NOT built by the Pallavas?
q.x: The Brihadisvara temple was built by Rajaraja Chola I.

q.s: The Undavalli cave temples near Vijayawada were excavated by the:
q.x: The Vishnukundins began Hindu cave temples in Telugu lands in the Pallava style.

q.s: The Kannada poet Ponna was patronised by the Rashtrakuta ruler:
q.x: Ponna was Krishna III's poet; Ranna was patronised by Tailapa II and Satyashraya.

q.s: Which of the following dynasty–capital pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Hoysala capital was Dwarasamudra; Devagiri was the Yadava capital.

q.s: Which Reddi ruler shifted the capital from Addanki to Kondavidu?
q.x: Anavota Reddy moved the capital to Kondavidu; Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the kingdom.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a capital of the Vijayanagara empire?
q.x: After Hampi, Vijayanagara capitals were Penugonda and Chandragiri; Kondavidu was a Reddi capital.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of the fall of the Kakatiya kingdom?
q.x: No European sea blockade figures among the causes of the Kakatiya fall in 1323.

q.s: The Kaluvacheru inscription of 1423 of the Reddi period was issued by:
q.x: Anitalli issued the Kaluvacheru inscription; Srinatha composed the Santana Sagaram tank inscription.

q.s: The first recorded use of firearms in India, against Vijayanagara around 1366-68, was by the:
q.x: The Bahmanis under Muhammad Shah I used firearms c. 1366-68; Babur only popularised field artillery.

q.s: Which ruler was the first to bear the title 'Andhra Suratrana'?
q.x: Kapaya Nayaka was the first holder of the title Andhra Suratrana.

q.s: Under the Kakatiyas, most of the Nayakas and officials came from:
q.x: The Sudra Kakatiyas drew their officials from warrior and peasant groups, so Brahmins lost political clout.

q.s: In the 17th century, the diamonds traded from the Andhra coast came mainly from:
q.x: Golconda was famous for diamonds; silk and cotton piece-goods came from Bengal.

q.s: The Ryotwari system in the Madras Presidency was introduced by:
q.x: Thomas Munro introduced Ryotwari; its over-assessment and cash payments led to land alienation.

q.s: Who was known as the 'Gokhale of South India'?
q.x: Mocherla Ramachandra Rao was the 'Gokhale of South India'.

q.s: In Andhra, the Swadeshi movement was popularly known as the:
q.x: Its Andhra phase (1906-11) was called the Vandemataram movement.

q.s: 'Gudisale Kalipotunnayi', which won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1975, was written by:
q.x: Boyi Bhimanna wrote it; Kundurti Anjaneyulu is called 'Vachana Kavitha Pitamaha'.

q.s: Who is called 'Vachana Kavitha Pitamaha' (father of free verse) in Telugu?
q.x: Kundurti Anjaneyulu bears the title.

q.s: During Gandhi's visit to Kakinada in April 1921, Durgabai Deshmukh arranged his meeting with:
q.x: Durgabai arranged his meeting with Devadasis and Muslim women and translated his speech.

q.s: Who was the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha, at Vedaranyam in 1930?
q.x: Rukmini Lakshmipathi was the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha.

q.s: The committee set up in 1952-53 to examine financial and other issues of forming Andhra State was headed by:
q.x: The Wanchoo Committee examined the problems; Nehru later ruled out Madras as the capital.

q.s: Krishna Patrika was founded in 1902 by:
q.x: Konda Venkatappayya founded Krishna Patrika; Mutnuri Krishna Rao later edited it.

q.s: At which Andhra Mahasabha were the Ceded Districts named 'Rayalaseema' in 1928?
q.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao gave the name at the Nandyal session (1928).

q.s: The Sribagh Pact of 1937 related to safeguards for:
q.x: The Sribagh Pact was signed to protect Rayalaseema's interests.

q.s: Which street dance-drama of Andhra is regarded as the forerunner of Kuchipudi?
q.x: Veedhi Natakam (Veedhi Bhagavatam) is seen as the forerunner of Kuchipudi.

q.s: The Velugu programme in Andhra Pradesh (2000) was later renamed:
q.x: Velugu, run by SERP, was renamed Indira Kranthi Patham.

q.s: Who was the first president of the Viplava Rachayitala Sangham (Virasam), founded in 1970?
q.x: Sri Sri was Virasam's first president.

q.s: 'Bhishma Pratigna' (1921), the first Telugu silent feature film, was made by:
o: Raghupathi Venkaiah Naidu and R.S. Prakash
q.x: Raghupathi Venkaiah Naidu and his son R.S. Prakash made it.

q.s: Which of the following film–maker pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Lava Kusa (1963) was directed by C. Pullaiah and C.S. Rao.

q.s: Which of the following Andhra Pradesh districts is NOT noted as a major source of Gulf emigration?
q.x: East Godavari, West Godavari and Kadapa are the major sources of Gulf migrants.

q.s: In 2015, which court banned the Jain practice of Santhara (Sallekhana)?
q.x: The Rajasthan High Court banned it; the Supreme Court stayed that ruling.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the changing Indian family is correct?
o: Industrialisation turns the family from a production unit into a consumption unit
Women's employment has reduced the number of female-headed households
The Hindu Succession Act has had no effect on family structure
Urbanisation has eliminated all emotional bonds of the joint family
q.x: The family has become a consumption unit; women's employment has raised female-headed households.

q.s: How many Scheduled Tribe communities are notified in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: There are 34 ST communities in the State; only part of them live in the Scheduled Areas.

q.s: Which of the following districts of Andhra Pradesh does NOT have Scheduled Areas?
q.x: Scheduled Areas lie in Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, ASR, Anakapalli and Eluru.

q.s: Which of the following tribe–State pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Gaddi are shepherds of Himachal Pradesh.

q.s: The PCPNDT Act, 1994 prohibits:
q.x: The Act regulates prenatal diagnosis, allowing medical uses but banning sex determination.

q.s: The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016 bars children below what age from all occupations, with exceptions?
q.x: It bars children below 14 from all work, matching the RTE age group (6-14); adolescents 14-18 are barred from hazardous work.

q.s: The anti-arrack movement (Sara Nishedha Udyamam) of 1991-92 in Andhra Pradesh was started by the rural women of:
q.x: It began with the women of Dubagunta village in Nellore district.

q.s: The 'Visakha Ukku – Andhrula Hakku' agitation of 1966 is associated with the fast of:
q.x: T. Amrutha Rao's fast led the agitation for the Visakhapatnam steel plant.

q.s: As per NFHS-5, which State has the highest share of women aged 20-24 married before 18?
q.x: West Bengal has the highest share; the all-India figure is 23.3%.
